intro: You are about to enter the Great Mosque of Bursa, a mosque and complex in Bursa province, built in 1396–1400. It is the masterpiece of the multi-domed plan: twenty domes carried on twelve piers. And at its centre stands a fountain, lit through an opening left where a dome would be.
history: Behind this building lies a promise. Bayezid I had vowed twenty mosques if he won at Nicopolis; on his return, he built one mosque with twenty domes instead. It was finished in 1400. Two years later, when Timur took Bursa, it was damaged, and afterwards it was repaired. Its fountain stands beneath the opening left where one of the domes would have been.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the twenty domes, the ablution fountain, the walnut minbar, the calligraphic panels and the two minarets.
facts: Did you know? More than 190 calligraphic panels cover its walls, most of them by nineteenth-century masters, so the mosque can be read as a museum of the art. The twenty domes stand in place of the twenty mosques Bayezid I had vowed for his victory at Nicopolis. And the fountain at the centre sits under the opening left where a dome would be: with no courtyard, the interior does the courtyard's work.
outro: This brings our tour of the Great Mosque of Bursa to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
